question: Your compliance team requires that no refund above $500 is ever processed without human approval. The system prompt of the support agent already states this rule clearly. In testing, however, the agent still called process_refund for amounts above $500 in about 3% of the cases. Which change best guarantees that the agent follows this rule?

options.text: Add few-shot examples to the system prompt that show the agent escalating refund requests above $500 to a human.
options.reason: Few-shot examples improve the behavior of the model but remain prompt-based, so they cannot guarantee compliance the way a hook can.

options.text: Instruct the agent to state the refund amount and confirm that it is within policy before it calls process_refund.
options.reason: A self-check instruction depends on the model following the prompt, so it gives probabilistic compliance and is not a deterministic guarantee.

options.text: Rewrite the refund rule in the system prompt with more emphatic wording and place it at the very start of the prompt.
options.reason: Stronger prompt wording is still prompt-based enforcement, which gives only probabilistic compliance, so some violations can still occur.

options.text: Add a hook that intercepts outgoing process_refund calls, blocks amounts above $500, and redirects the case to escalate_to_human.
options.reason: A tool call interception hook enforces the business rule deterministically, so it gives the guaranteed compliance that the rule requires.
